industry: Veterinary clinics, pet hospitals, urgent/ER, boarding/daycare, grooming, and related pet services
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'Specialist' / 'board-certified' / 'board eligible' unless the veterinarian currently holds and maintains certification from an AVMA ABVS-recognized specialty organization (AVMA PVME); use 'practice limited to' when not certified
'Cure' / disease-outcome guarantees for animals without substantiation; testimonials that imply typical medical results (FTC 16 CFR 255; AVMA PVME)
'$X value' on free exams unless that is the price actually charged (16 CFR 233/251) (common on GOLD-vet-pet-001/006/017)
Stacking five+ unrelated coupon circles on the front that bury the hero offer (GOLD-vet-pet-001/039 pattern vs roofing round-5 one-offer preference)
Advertising DEA controlled substances (opioids, ketamine, etc.) as consumer mail offers; keep drug talk to general preventive categories only when legally marketable
'Fear-Free' / trademarked certifications unless the practice actually holds them
Fake scarcity on boarding ('only 2 spots') unless capacity is truly limited
compliance_notes: AVMA Principles of Veterinary Medical Ethics: advertising must not be false, deceptive, or misleading (including by material omission); testimonials should be readily verifiable; follow FTC endorsement guides; 'specialist' reserved for current board certification; no 'board eligible/qualified'.
State veterinary boards add advertising rules (varies by state); verify local rules before 'best vet', superiority, or guarantee language.
FTC Act s.5 + 16 CFR 255 (2023) + Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule: real clients, material connections disclosed, typical-results implied by testimonials.
16 CFR 251/233: 'free' and former-price/'value' claims need real regular prices and clear conditions next to the offer.
Wellness-plan auto-renewals: disclose price, what's included, how to cancel (ROSCA for online signup; state ARL where applicable, e.g. California).
Children's photos of kids with pets need parent consent; pet photos of clients need owner permission.
Do not imply government endorsement or official 'pet census' mail (39 USC 3001).
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, love, relief, belonging are all options when they fit and stay legal; the client chooses.
Every angle and every emotion_by_offer combo carries a sell_the_outcome_line.
Unverified (agency-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold fronts often stack 4–6 coupon circles (GOLD-vet-pet-001/039/055) vs roofing round-5 preference for one clear offer
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: No vet votes yet; default to one hero offer on the front and secondary offers on the back; Patrick's votes override once they exist.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: 'Board-certified' / 'specialist' language in some clinic marketing vs AVMA PVME specialty rules
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: only current ABVS-recognized diplomates use specialist/board-certified; others use 'practice limited to'.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Vendor-published ROI/response on PostcardMania/OMNI cases vs need for verified evidence
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Label agency-only unverified; never print those numbers on client cards as proof.
